transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I just can't stop thinking about my face. The left side of it just looks off. My nose and my jaw are crooked, and it's really obvious in every ID photo or whenever I have my camera on for my online classes. 

People tell me they don't see it when I bring it up, but... I know it's there. I feel like everyone in the CNC lab is noticing it before they even look at my work. It's just constantly on my mind and I don't know how to stop focusing on it.
Do you find yourself spending a lot of time repeatedly checking your face in mirrors or other reflective surfaces throughout the day?

Yeah, I do. Especially before I leave for school. I get... stuck, I guess, just checking my face in the bathroom mirror. And then I'll pull up my phone camera to check it there, too. I spend a lot of time trying to fix my hair or changing my shirt, just trying to find a way to hide the angle of my jaw. 

I keep asking my mom if it looks weird, too. Honestly, sometimes I do all this for so long that I end up missing my lab completely. Or if I do finally make it in, I show up so wiped out from stressing over it that I can't even focus on my work.
Deep down, do you ever feel that your face might actually look completely normal and that your mind could be exaggerating it, or are you completely convinced it really is deformed?

I... I don't really know. I mean, I hear people when they tell me they don't see it, but I don't feel like my mind is making it up or exaggerating anything. When I look in the mirror or at a photo, it's just right there. I see it. So, yeah, I guess I'm pretty convinced it really is crooked. I don't see how it could just be in my head.
When you are around others, do you believe people are actually talking about, mocking, or reacting to your face, or is it more of a worry that they might notice it?

I think it's more of a worry. I don't really hear people whispering about me or anything like that, and no one has ever made fun of me to my face. It's just... I feel like they must be noticing it. Like when I'm in the lab, I just get this overwhelming feeling that they're looking at my jaw or my nose, even if they aren't saying anything. So, no, I don't think they're actively mocking me, I just worry a lot that they see how crooked it is.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with persistent preoccupation with a perceived physical defect (asymmetry/crookedness of the nose and jaw) that others do not notice. This is accompanied by repetitive checking behaviors (mirror checking, phone camera checks), camouflaging efforts, reassurance seeking, and significant functional impairment (missing academic labs). Insight is poor but not frank psychosis or persecutory delusion, fitting ICD-10 F45.2 (Body dysmorphic disorder / Dysmorphophobia non-delusional).

confirmed_symptoms: Persistent preoccupation with perceived defect/crookedness in nose and jaw
Belief that the asymmetry is noticeable to others despite reassurance
Frequent and prolonged mirror and phone camera checking
Attempts to camouflage perceived defect with hair and clothing

additional_requirements: Absence of frank persecutory or referential delusions confirmed
